title: SageCare: Runtime Healing of Superfluous Storage Fetches
problem: Memory-intensive applications generate unnecessary prefetch requests that waste bandwidth and degrade performance. Current prefetching policies do not adapt to runtime memory access patterns.
motivation: Eliminating wasted prefetch traffic can significantly improve memory system efficiency and reduce overall system latency.
method: SageCare monitors memory access patterns at runtime to identify superfluous storage fetches. The system adaptively adjusts prefetching policies based on observed behavior to minimize unnecessary traffic. This dynamic approach allows the system to respond to changing application phases.
key_novelty: Runtime adaptive prefetch policy adjustment based on dynamically detected memory access patterns rather than static policies.
contributions: Runtime detection mechanism for identifying superfluous storage fetches
Evaluation showing improved performance on memory-intensive workloads
